objective: Read the primary report this lab's cylinder shedding gate is filmed against and record which of the two circulating Strouhal correlations it actually supports at a Reynolds number of 100, then either re-attribute the constants or re-grade the act
rationale: A filmed gate grades the unsteady cylinder act as a pass at 0.77 percent against a correlation named on screen for two published authors. The constants behind that pass are attributed by the repository to its own task prompt rather than to any paper, and the one form the repository does cite to a paper disagrees materially: executed arithmetic at a Reynolds number of 100 gives 0.158994 for the form actually used, a pass at 0.75 percent against the measured value, and 0.167056 for the cited form, which is a miss at 5.54 percent. Both forms circulate in the cylinder literature for different Reynolds ranges, so which one governs here is a source question and not a classification one, and it cannot be settled by any amount of internal consistency checking. This is the smallest complete instance of the referent travelling with the verdict, the clause adopted today, and it sits on a camera surface. The same reading closes a second item behind it: the correlation is duplicated inline in a second module, in a file whose sibling states in its own comment that it is deliberately not duplicated because two copies is how a gate silently drifts. That repair is blocked only because re-attributing the constants would otherwise have to be done twice
gate: Two-valued on the primary source, with the third value reserved for the honest failure. SUPPORTED if the report gives the form actually used, with those constants, over a Reynolds range that includes 100: the gate's attribution is then correct, the constants are re-cited to the report, and the act stands at 0.77 percent. NOT SUPPORTED if the report gives only the other form, or gives the used form over a range excluding 100: the act is then re-graded against whatever the report supports, and if that regrade is a miss it is published as a miss. NOT OBTAINED if the report cannot be read: the gate then carries an explicit face caveat that its constant has no cited source, which is its true present state, and the item closes as a recorded failure to obtain rather than as an open question. IDENTITY TEST, per Verification Charter 2a. Q1, what makes this FAIL: the report supporting the other form at this Reynolds number. Q2, could a wrong treatment still pass? A check that compared our arithmetic against our own constants would pass with the attribution entirely wrong, which is precisely the state the gate is in today and precisely why the only admissible evidence here is the report itself. No internal check can substitute. EXTERNAL REFERENT, per Verification Charter 6a: the report itself, an independent published source that this lab did not write, obtained from the public archive that hosts it. Nothing else counts for this item.
cost_basis: Zero solver compute, and no solve is needed for either outcome: the measured shedding value is already extracted and on the record, so a regrade is one division. The arithmetic that established the size of the discrepancy, 0.158994 against 0.167056 at a Reynolds number of 100, was itself carried out host side at zero compute during the referent audit, which is the direct precedent for the price. The cost is agent time on obtaining and reading one report
expected_knowledge_gain: A filmed number stops resting on a constant with no cited source. That is the whole gain and it is enough: the surface is one Katie films, the discrepancy between the two candidate forms is seven times the passing margin, and the failure mode is that a viewer reads a published attribution over a house constant. Behind it, the duplicated inline copy of the same correlation becomes repairable in one pass instead of two. There is a general form worth more than the instance, and it is why this is filed rather than left as a chore: this lab found the defect by asking what a number was checked against, not by checking the number, and the same question has not been asked of the other correlations on that surface
hard_criterion_note: Starts no flow case. A regrade uses a measured value already on the record
